reviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience at this mosque. As a Shia Muslim, I once went there to pray Jumu’ah, and I immediately felt uncomfortable because I noticed numerous people staring at me as though I had done something wrong.

After Jumu’ah, five Sunni Muslims approached me. Three of them mocked me, while the other two tried to convince me to convert to Sunni Islam. What made the situation even more upsetting was that several other people were nearby, yet no one stepped in or said anything.

I always believed that, regardless of our differences in schools of thought, Muslims are supposed to treat one another as brothers and sisters. Unfortunately, this experience made me question whether I would feel welcomed or respected there again.

People can have different beliefs and practices, but that should never be an excuse to disrespect or ridicule someone. We should be able to worship peacefully and treat one another with dignity and respect.

reviews.text:
I am writing this review with respect and sincerity. Cleanliness is a fundamental part of Islam, and a mosque should reflect that value.

Unfortunately, during my visit to Alshareef Islamic Centre, the washrooms were not clean and had a very strong unpleasant smell. It was difficult to make wudu properly because of the odor. In addition, the carpets inside the prayer area also had a bad smell, which made it uncomfortable to pray.

A mosque is a place of worship, purity, and peace. I sincerely request the management to take cleanliness seriously, especially the washrooms and carpets, so worshippers can pray with comfort and khushu.

Please improve the cleanliness of the mosque.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
We are truly sorry about this. We had a cleaner but he travelled, and we've been looking for a cleaner (paid) for the past two weeks.

Our most sincere apologies for the current situation. We will rectify it immediately. 

Jazakum Allah Khair for bringing this to our attention. 

We hope next time you visit you'll find it as pleasant as every other Musalli was used to seeing in our little humble abode.
